annotation.kind: source selection, Algorithm 3.1 execution semantics, tier label, and exact finite-index restatement of Theorem 3.2

assumptions: The matrix dimensions m, n, and t and block dimensions b1, b, and b2 are positive.
The block counts p, q, and r are positive and satisfy m = p*b1, n = q*b, and t = r*b2.
Both inputs are converted componentwise to the low precision through standard relative errors bounded by uLow.

The block-FMA output unit roundoff is one of the paper's low/high formats, with uHigh <= uLow; Algorithm 3.1's final working/output roundoff is an independent nonnegative precision parameter, and the internal unit roundoff satisfies uBar <= uFma.
Every computed output entry is the final state of a linked q-block P04BlockFmaDotRun over the corresponding converted row and column.
Each entry trace starts at zero and satisfies the local recurrence (3.2), including its primitive error bounds, evaluation-order semantics, and equation (3.3)'s prioritized effective roundoff.
The two relevant gamma denominators are positive.
The finite-real standard model excludes underflow, overflow, exceptional IEEE values, and the second output rounding omitted in the paper's analysis.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P04 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P04 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p04_t2_mixed_input_product_bound {m n t b1 b b2 p q r : ℕ} (run : P04MixedInputMatMulRun m n t b1 b b2 p q r) : ∀ i j, |run.computed i j - p04RectMatMul run.A run.B i j| ≤ (2*run.uLow + run.uLow^2 + p04BlockFmaCoeff (p04EffectiveFmaRoundoff run.uBar run.uFma run.uOut) run.uBar q n * (1+run.uLow)^2) * p04AbsRectMatMul run.A run.B i j
formal_statement.plain_language: For every entry of the rectangular matrix product produced by Algorithm 3.1 after low-precision input conversion, the absolute forward error is bounded by Theorem 3.2's exact coefficient times the corresponding entry of |A||B|.

informal_proof: For each output entry, unroll the linked recurrence and apply the accumulated-product lemma to construct the alpha and beta factors, obtaining the exact block-FMA coefficient. Bound each converted input by (1+uLow) times its original magnitude, producing the squared factor. Separately expand the two relative input conversions to obtain 2*uLow+uLow^2, apply the finite-summation perturbation bound, and add the two componentwise errors.
informal_statement: The full finite-index componentwise form of Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6) for Algorithm 3.1.
